profile.size: Up to 50+ lb; Florida record 90 lb
profile.diet: Herrings, threadfin shad, menhaden, jack, and squid
profile.behavior: Migratory coastal pelagic schooling predator. Moves south to Florida in winter following water temp and bait runs.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside the preferred temperature range for king mackerel.
factors.value_notes: NOAA and SAFMC report that king mackerel prefer warm water and seldom occur below about 20 °C (68 °F). This supports a lower thermal boundary, but does not establish the configured 20–29 °C outer range or 22–26 °C ideal interval as a preferred-temperature curve; the upper bound and ideal band remain unvalidated.

factors.reason_template: Thermal break strength is {per10km} C per 10 km, where bait concentrations draw kings.
factors.value_notes: The generic FWC homepage citation does not support a numeric or monotonic SST-gradient response for king mackerel. Warm-water affinity and seasonal migration do not demonstrate that sharper satellite SST gradients improve habitat suitability. Keep the factor's existing configuration unchanged, but treat its evidence claim as unsupported pending species-specific front/gradient research.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in coastal shelf waters where kings hunt.
factors.value_notes: NOAA reports adult habitat at roughly 35–183 m; the Florida Museum reports 23–34 m and FishBase a broader 5–140 m depth range. These sources confirm coastal-pelagic shelf use but differ in depth coverage and do not validate the configured 10–100 m band or 15–45 m ideal as a single preferred range.

value_text.peak: It is peak king mackerel season in South Florida.
value_text.off: It is outside the main king mackerel season.

factors.value_notes: NOAA documents a winter mixing zone south of the Florida Keys from November through March, and seasonal north/south migration; the Florida Museum describes seasonal stock mixing patterns in South Florida. This supports a South Florida winter presence window, but does not validate the exact November–April months or December–March peak scores as catch probabilities.

text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.

timing.note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.
